title: AgentPack
description: AgentPack: the versioned, attestation-signed bundle that tenants install from the agent-pack registry + catalog (EPIC-00 issue #4; issue #40). A pack bundles registry artifacts (profile + personas + prompts + policy + tool manifests) behind one immutable, schema-validated, publisher-attested document. Field vocabulary is consumed from the harvested CMR module.schema.json (schema const identity, dependencies/consumers crossref model), shared-frontend modules/schema.json (id/category/status/upstream), and CMR registry/events (closed registry event kinds). Lifecycle values are the pack registry states: planned -> live -> paused -> retired. The closed platform vocabularies live in registry/packs/pack-catalog.yaml; this schema embeds the same ids in definitions enums and registry/packs/validate.py runs a schema<->catalog parity gate so the two can never drift. Pack snapshots are immutable and recorded in registry/packs/versions/manifest.yaml; each published snapshot carries a signed attestation block (RSA-PSS / PS256) verified by validate.py and, at install time, by registry/packs/installer.py (consumer trust).

schema.description: Pack schema version identity. Exactly 'agent-pack/v1' for v1; evolution happens via a new version identity, never silently (CMR ADR-0003 pattern).

id.description: Stable pack id (lowercase, dash-separated, e.g. worker-platform). Must equal the release filename stem <id>.<version>.yaml.

version.description: SemVer X.Y.Z of THIS pack snapshot. A published (id, version) is immutable: once recorded in versions/manifest.yaml the file is sha256-locked and cannot be edited.

name.description: Human-readable pack name shown in the catalog.

category.description: Catalog grouping for the pack (closed vocabulary from pack-catalog.yaml, e.g. coding, data, orchestration, review, research, security, integration).

upstream.description: Source repository URI of the pack (provenance; shared-frontend 'upstream' field).

publisher.description: Accountable publisher of the pack lifecycle, namespace/team (consumes the profile 'owner' semantic, e.g. platform/execution). The attestation kid binds to the publisher's public key.

lifecycle.description: Lifecycle state of this pack snapshot in the registry (planned -> live -> paused -> retired). Only 'live' packs are installable. Current registry state is driven by PackRegistry transitions; this field records the state at snapshot time.

description.description: Optional human-readable description shown in the catalog.

tags.description: Free-form search tags for the catalog.

dependencies.description: Other packs this pack depends on, pinned by (id, version) — the catalog crossref source. Dependents of a pack are computed by PackRegistry.crossref.

contents.description: Contents manifest: the bundled registry artifacts this pack installs, grouped by artifact type (profile/persona/prompt/policy/tool). Each entry is self-contained (base64 data) with a pinned sha256 so install/drift detection is mechanical and offline.

attestation.description: Publisher attestation over the pack's canonical JSON (every field except attestation.signature). Consumer trust: installer.py refuses a pack whose signature is missing or does not verify against the publisher public key.

kid.description: Key id of the signing key (e.g. ao-pack-publisher-v1). The verifier selects the matching public key.

alg.description: Signature algorithm. PS256 = RSA-PSS with SHA-256 (RSASSA-PSS).

signedAt.description: UTC signing timestamp, RFC 3339 second precision (e.g. 2026-09-08T12:00:00Z).

signature.description: Base64-encoded RSASSA-PSS signature over the canonical JSON of the pack (attestation.signature excluded from the signed payload).

categoryId.description: Closed pack category vocabulary. Keep in sync with pack-catalog.yaml categories (validate.py parity gate enforces it).

artifactType.description: Closed artifact types a pack may bundle. Keep in sync with pack-catalog.yaml artifactTypes (validate.py parity gate enforces it).

lifecycleState.description: Pack registry lifecycle states: planned -> live -> paused -> retired (shared-frontend status vocabulary consumed: planned/live/paused/retired).

artifactEntry.description: One bundled artifact. ref is the artifact id (e.g. coder@1.0.0 for a profile seed, coder for a persona card, coder/primary@v1 for a prompt module, worker-bundle for a policy bundle, gh_issue for a tool); data is the base64 artifact content; sha256 is the digest of the decoded data (install + drift detection verify it).

ref.description: Artifact reference within the owning lane's vocabulary.

sha256.description: Hex sha256 of the decoded data bytes.
